resources.title: Reading for maximum retention and recall (intensive reading)
resources.description: Theme: READING JSS 1 | Content: 1. Reading from passages for maximum recall on: - diet and nutrition, including addition of nutrients, like Vitamin A in sugar and iodine in salt, - safety of packaged water . 2. Reading strategies e.g., preview, question, recite, recall, review, (SPQ3R)
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. preview passages; 2. read carefully a given passage; 3. recall salient points in a given passage; 4. review the passage.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the need for, and value of a flexible reading strategy, which allows for previewing, intensive or concentrated reading, repeated reading and active recall (self recitation), or essential facts and information. 2. Shows students how to apply some reading strategies adopted for use in schools. 3. Asks questions on the ideas contained in the passage.

Students: 1. Preview the reading materials by reading the main ideas which have been developed or amplified 2. Read the passage. 3. Recall mentally or record notes on the salient points, or the main ideas. 4. Reread the given passage and the relevant questions for maximum retention and recall. 5. Practise more exercises.
resources.resources: 1. Passages 2. Magazines and newspaper cuttings. 3. Selections from other subject areas. 4. Recommended text/supplementary readers.
resources.assessment: Students to : 1. preview passages correctly; 2. correctly read given passages; 3. recall correctly salient points in passages given; 4. review passages; and 5. practise more exercises.

resources.title: Reading for main and supporting ideas
resources.description: Theme: READING JSS 1 | Content: 1. Identifying main and supporting ideas in a given passage- a passage relating to automobiles. 2. Differentiating between main and supporting ideas in a given passage.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. Identify main and supporting ideas in a ideas from a given passage; and 2. Differentiate between main and supporting ideas from a given passage;
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Selects a passage relating to automobiles (road safety). 2. Guides pupils to read and re-read the passage. 3. Guides pupils to identify main and supporting ideas in the passage. 4. Explains the differences between main and supporting ideas.

Students: 1. Read and re-read the passage. 2. Work in pairs or groups to identify main or Supporting ideas in assigned paragraphs. 3. Make group presentation during plenary. 4. write main and supporting ideas in exercise books.
resources.resources: 1.Selected passage from the subject area on automobiles (road safety), 2.Motor vehicle; real or drawing 3.Pictorial aids 4.Course book
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. identify accurately main and supporting ideas; and 2. differentiate between main and supporting ideas.

resources.title: Reading to answer specific questions
resources.description: Theme: READING JSS 1 | Content: 1.Reading and answering specific questions that address different kinds of questions on issues highlighting: - Knowledge level - Translation level - Interpretation level - Projection level 2.Other types of questions e.g. - Explanation question. - Discussion questions - Questions that require conclusions to be drawn - Questions that require them to make projections. - Questions that will elicit students‘ opinion.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to read given selected passages and answer specific questions.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Selects suitable contemporary passages. 2. Draws suitable comprehension questions on selected passages. 3. Groups students for purpose of further practice Note: The practice questions the teacher draws should cover all levels of comprehension e.g., (1) Where (2) When (3) How (4) Why (5) What

Students: 1. Read selected materials on contemporary issues. 2. Respond to teacher‘s questions on passages read. 3. Work in groups developing and answering questions on given materials. 4. Answer questions on all levels of comprehension.
resources.resources: 1. Selections from other subject areas 2. Newspapers /Magazine cuttings. 3. Recommended text 4 .Advertisement 5. Supplementary readers
resources.assessment: Students to answer accurately questions developed by the teacher covering the four levels of comprehension and other types of questions.

resources.title: Reading to understand the author‘s mood.
resources.description: Theme: READING JSS 1 | Content: Reading to understand author‘s mood e.g. anger, happiness, doubt, disappointment, suspicion, excitement, etc.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to : 1. identify the author‘s mood through use of words and expressions; 2. read between lines with a view to detecting hidden attitude; and 3. identify the general impression created by the author‘s manner of presentation.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Selects materials and presents them for students to read. 2. Guides students to identify author‘s mood through words and expressions. 3. Guides students to read between the lines with a view to detecting hidden attitudes. 4. Guides the students to identify the overall impression created by the author‘s style of presentation.

Students: 1. Read materials presented to them by the teacher. 2. Identify author‘s mood through words and expressions encountered from the passage. 3. Read between the lines in order to detect author‘s hidden attitudes. 4. Identify the overall impression through extensive practice.
resources.resources: 1. Recommended text. 2. Supplementary readers. 3. Newspapers and magazine cuttings
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. identify correctly words and expressions that point to author‘s mood from given passages; 2. identify underlying (hidden) meaning/attitude; and 3. identify accurately the author‘s method of presentation (objective /balanced, biased, care-free, verbose and terse etc).

resources.title: Reading to interpret diagrams, maps and sketches
resources.description: Theme: READING JSS 1 | Content: 1. Reading to interpret diagrams, maps and sketches accurately. 2. Making meaning from spatial description/ presentation. 3. Identifying how a given diagram or map clarifies or complements written material.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. read and interpret diagrams and maps accurately; 2. make meaning from spatial description/ Presentation; and 3. identify how a given diagram or map clarifies/comple ments written material.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Presents suitable materials in form of passages, selections, maps, sketches for students‘ analysis and description as well as extensive practices. 2. Guides students to associate sketches with written texts. 3. Guides students to anticipate questions that could emerge from given texts or sketches.

Students: 1. Read selected materials and answer questions to guide interpretation. 2. Practise associating sketches with written texts. 3. Work in groups or pairs to anticipate, ask and answer questions that could emerge from given texts and sketches/ diagrams. 4. Practise identifying paragraphs with the appropriate sketches.
resources.resources: 1. Selected sketches, passages, maps. 2. Selections from subject areas. 3. Advertisements, etc.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. read and interpret maps, sketches and diagrams accurately; 2. explain appropriately, illustrations /maps or sketches provided by the teacher; 3. explain/describe adequately, relationship between a given passage and a sketch; and 4. provide appropriate illustrations for given paragraphs.

resources.title: Reading to follow direction in written communication
resources.description: Theme: READING JSS 1 | Content: 1. Reading to follow direction in written communication. 2. Identifying key words in the passage that signal direction. 3. Blending material with related sketch.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. read given selections in order to follow direction; 2. identify key words in the passage that signal direction; and 3. blend reading material with related sketch.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Selects and presents appropriate materials. 2. Guides students to identify the possible instructions and/or direction, 3. Presents maps and leads students to arrive at particular destinations. 4. Guides students to identify key words that signal direction. 5. Prepares and gives directions for students to practice.

Students: 1. Read materials presented by the teacher. 2. practise identification of key words related to directions e.g., `moving from left to right‘, East to West‘, `Northwards‘ ‗Southwards‘, `Upwards‘, `towards‘, etc. 3. Practise identification of direction in response to teacher‘s prompting. 4. Practise with maps presented by the teacher. 5. Practise teacher‘s and students‘ initiated directions.
resources.resources: 1. Selected passages 2. Invitation cards. 3. Do-it-yourself manual. 4. Maps. 5. Selections from other subject areas.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. respond correctly to questions that are instruction based; and 2. prepare accurately directions: -from their homes to the school; - from their class room to the principal‘s office; -from the main gate to their class room.

resources.title: Writing to Highlight Main and Supporting Ideas.
resources.description: Theme: WRITING JSS 1 | Content: 1. Story or passage highlighting main and supporting ideas, 2. Arrangement of ideas in logical sequence with introduction, and conclusion.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. read through a topic; 2. jot down main and supporting ideas as they occur; 3. arrange the ideas in a logical sequence; and 4. write appropriate introduction and effective conclusion;
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Presents story or passage to students. 2. Exemplifies outlines using the story or passage. 2. Leads the students to identify main and supporting ideas. 3. Leads the students to re-arrange all the ideas they had produced or had written in logical sequence. 4. Leads the students to identify appropriate introduction and conclusion for selected topics.

Students: 1. Read the story or passage provided. 2. Identify the outline of story on passage. 3. Write down the main and supporting ideas. 4. Arrange ideas in logical sequence. 5. Write appropriate introduction and conclusion on selected passages based on the outline.
resources.resources: 1. Model essays. 2. Story books. 3. Passages 4. Feature articles on contemporary issues. 5. Textbooks, course books on other subject areas.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. read given materials accurately; 2. jot down appropriately main and supporting ideas; 3. arrange correctly the ideas in logical sequence; and 4. write correctly appropriate introduction and conclusion;

resources.title: Composition Writing: Narrative and Descriptive
resources.description: Theme: WRITING JSS 1 | Content: 1. The history of the FRSC. 2. Aims of the FRSC i.e. evolving safer road culture in Nigeria.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. read through the topic; 2. jot down main and supporting ideas; 3. write the history of the Federal Road Safety Commission (FRSC); and 4. state the aims of the FRSC.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads students to read the passage on the Federal Road Safety Commission. 2. Guides students to trace the history of the FRSC. 3. States the aims of the FRSC.

Students: 1. Listen to the teacher‘s presentation of the passage. 2. Participate in tracing the history of the FRSC. 3. Write down the aims of the FRSC as stated by the teacher.
resources.resources: 1. Relevant passages on the topic. 2. Other literature e.g. FRSC Act.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain the history of the FRSC; and 2. state three aims of the FRSC.

resources.title: Letter Writing: Features of Informal and Formal Letters
resources.description: Theme: WRITING JSS 1 | Content: Letter Writing: i. Types - Formal - Informal ii. Format Formal Letters: They have conventional forms of two addresses, opening salutation, correct heading, body of the letter, closing and signature. Informal Letter: One address, opening salutation, body of the letter and closing.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. identify the types of letters; 2. identify the different formats of letters; and 3. write different types of letters to suit different situations;
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides students to identify types and formats of letters. 2. Leads students to discuss types and formats of letters. 3. Writes a model format. 4. Guides students to write a formal and informal letter.

Students: 1. Identify types and formats of letters. 2. Discuss types and formats of letters. 3. Copy teacher‘s model. 4. Write a formal and informal letter.
resources.resources: 1. Sample letters (formal and informal). 2. Newspaper/ magazine cuttings. 3. Textbooks.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. identify types and formats of letters; and 2. write different types of letters (formal and informal) to suit different situations;

resources.title: Speeches: Production of vowel and consonant sounds in passages
resources.description: Theme: LISTENING AND SPEAKING JSS 1 | Content: 1. Vowels and Consonant Sounds 2. Listening to speeches based on the following: - The family - The school - Places of worship - Consumer, market and society - Transportation - Health issues and epidemics e. g HIV/AIDS, malaria, polio, tetanus, meningitis etc. - Safety on the roads. - Corruption - Tribalism - Drug Abuse - Child labour and trafficking
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. re-tell what they have listened to; 2. explain key words and expressions on what they have listened to; 3. answer questions on what they have listened to; and 4. summarize what they have listened to.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Reads materials on topics under content column 2. Leads discussion on selected topics under content. 3. Develops and organizes students for play-lets on selected topics 4. Invites guest speakers to talk on chosen topics where applicable. 5. Presents recorded materials for more discussion. 6. Organises debates for the students 7. Organises impromptu speeches

Students: 1. Listen to the teacher‘s reading of selected materials. 2. Discuss the selected topics with the teacher. 3. Participate in play- lets on selected topics. 4. Listen to guest speakers and ask questions. 5. Listen to recorded materials and ask questions. 6. Participate in debates. 7. Participate in impromptu speeches
resources.resources: 1. Story books. 2. Magazines and newspaper cuttings on relevant topics. 3. Other resources. e.g. recorded tapes, radio broadcast etc.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1.re-tell the stories/speeches they have listened to; 2. explain some keywords and expressions; 3. answer questions on what they have listened to; and 4. summarize stories/passages/p resentations.

resources.title: Listening to and producing different speeches with reference to vowel sounds.
resources.description: Theme: LISTENING AND SPEAKING JSS 1 | Content: 1. Sentences, paragraphs, passages, plays, poems, should form the content for highlighting the sounds involved. 2. Long and short vowels e.g. sleep/slip; port/pot; leave/live these/this; sport/spot; cord/cod; forks/fox. 3. Consonants e.g. Back/pack, pull/ fool, Goat/toad, road/ load, things/ tins Thought/taught; Then/ den; Fox/box; voice/boys; chaos as in /k/ in chemist 4. vowel sounds e.g. /˄ /bus, /Ͻ /pot, holiday, boss, /a/ cat, hat, /a:/ father, cart, chart.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. listen to and produce different speeches with reference to long and short vowel sounds; 2. listen to and produce different speeches with reference to consonants.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Identifies/ produces materials for the correct pronunciation of the target sounds in context. 2. Emphasizes the correct articulatory movements in the pronunciation of the sounds.

Students: 1. Listen to the teacher and imitate the production of the sounds in context. 2. Practice the articulation of the sounds emphasized by the teacher in context
resources.resources: 1. Recorded materials e.g. audio and video tapes. 2. Newspaper/magazine cuttings and Supplementary readers containing passages on: - The family - The school - Places of worship - Consumer, market and society - Transportation - Health issues and epidemics e. g HIV/AIDS, malaria, polio, tetanus, meningitis etc. - Safety on the roads - Corruption - Tribalism - Drug Abuse - Child labour and - trafficking.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. identify correctly, long and short vowels in given sentences and selections; 2. identify correctly consonant sounds occurring in the given materials in context; and 3. identify the appropriate vowel sounds in passages/ plays/poems.

resources.title: Listening to and producing different speeches with reference consonant clusters and diphthongs.
resources.description: Theme: LISTENING AND SPEAKING JSS 1 | Content: 1. Consonant clusters e.g. desks, asks, sickle, plants, planks, subject, barns, drive, school, respect, sprinkle, attacked, string, throw, please, principle, trick, strive, thrive, truth, amplify, apple, tactile, splash, spread, struggle, streams, strong, scream, screen, shutter, scatter. 2. Diphthongs e.g. /ei/ as in: Mary /Meiri/, gate / geit/ ); day (/dei/); grey, they; pain: rain, train, slate, mate, weight; /ou/ as in: so, go, no, old, gold, told, sold, /Ͻi/ as in oil, boil, toil, coil; /uә / tour, sure. 3. Weak forms e.g. after, often, listen, sister, above, away, later, alone, abound, about.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. listen to and produce different speeches with reference to vowel sounds; 2. listen to and identify/ produce different speeches paying special attention to consonant clusters; 3. listen to different speeches with particular reference to diphthongs.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Stresses the distinction exemplified in minimal pairs 2. Initiates language games for practising different sounds. 3. Dictates short sentences containing the sounds. 4. Directs students to tell stories, paying attention to specified pairs.

Students: 1. Practise the differences in sounds exemplified in minimal pairs 2. Engage in language games as practice in relevant sounds. 3. Write sentences containing the sounds. 4. Tell stories paying attention to specified pairs
resources.resources: 1. Language games 2. Poems 3. Sentence strips 4. Other relevant resources e.g. pictures, real drawings, as bases for activities.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1.identify and pronounce correctly the relevant consonant clusters in paragraphs and selections; 2. identify and produce correctly the selected diphthongs in passages and speeches; 3. identify weak forms correctly in speeches and selections.

resources.title: Listening to and producing different speeches with reference to word boundaries, compound words and phrases.
resources.description: Theme: LISTENING AND SPEAKING JSS 1 | Content: 1. Word boundaries e.g. linking sounds: - matter of, fore-head, go-away, order of merit, butter and bread, leader of, Shar of Iran, pair of, fear of God, poor and blind, transfer of. 2. Compound words e.g. blackboard, ice-cream, swimming pool, lifelong, age old, teapot, classroom, night flight, return ticket, return journey, return flight, sister-in-law, dining room, market square. 3. Phrases e.g. a company of friends, a man of the people, a crop of ideas, a queue of traffic, a team of players, a basket of fruits, a set of furniture, a range of opinions, a row of houses, a chain of problems.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. listen to different speeches with particular reference to weak forms; 2. listen to different speeches paying attention to word boundaries; 3. listen to different speeches with special reference to compound words; 4. listen to different speeches paying attention to phrases.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Engages students in pair activities with reference to word boundaries. 2. organizes class discussions/play lets/ 3. Provides cues 4. Initiates activities 5. Responds to students‘ cues.

Students: 1. Participate in discussion/play lets/drama using question tags. 2. Follow cues 3. Participate in activities 4. Initiate cues
resources.resources: 1. Language games 2. Poems 3. Sentence strips 4. Other relevant resources e.g. pictures, real drawings, as bases for activities.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. identify correctly and produce accurately word boundaries; 2. identify and use correctly compound words in passages and selections; 3. identify correctly phrases in passages, selections and use them effectively in sentences.

resources.title: Questions and Question Tags
resources.description: Theme: LISTENING AND SPEAKING JSS 1 | Content: 1. Questions and their tags e.g. - Okoro: Teachers are always punctual, aren‘t they? - Ibrahim: Yes, they are. - Teacher: Okocha is the best footballer in Africa, isn‘t he? - Student: Yes, he is. - Student: The president of Nigeria is a powerful man, isn‘t he? - Student: Yes, he is. - Student: Some drivers drive too fast, don‘t they? - Student: Yes, they do.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to listen to different speeches with particular reference to questions and their tags.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Engages students in pair activities with reference to questions and their tags. 2. organizes class discussions 3. Provides cues 4. Initiates activities 5. Responds to students‘ cues.

Students: 1. Participate in discussion using question tags. 2. Follow cues 3. Participate in activities 4. Initiate cues
resources.resources: 1. Language games 2. Poems 3. Sentence strips 4. Other relevant resources e.g. pictures, real drawings, as bases for activities.
resources.assessment: Students to respond correctly to statements, utterances with reference to question tags.

resources.title: Listening Comprehension
resources.description: Theme: LISTENING AND SPEAKING JSS 1 | Content: 1. Listening for main ideas from selected passages on: - The family - The school - Places of worship - Consumer, market and society - Transportation - Health issues and epidemics e. g HIV/AIDS, - malaria, polio, tetanus, cleanliness, meningitis etc - Safety on the roads. - Corruption - Drug Abuse - Abuse of herbal medicines - Misuse of pesticides - Child labour and - trafficking - Global warming 2. Positioning of main ideas in given passages: beginning, middle or end.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to : 1. listen to given passages; and 2. extract main ideas from given passages.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Selects appropriate passages and materials. 2. Explains the meaning of main ideas. 3. Illustrates with specific examples. 4. Asks students to read selected passages and materials in class. 5. Guides the students to identify and extract the main ideas of a sentence or topic sentence 6. Explains the relative positions of main ideas of sentences in the different passages.

Students: 1. Pay attention and practise with examples given 2. Read selected passages and materials provided. 3. Practise the main idea identified from the text. 4. Practise and ask questions
resources.resources: 1. Essays written by teachers and students on the relevant topics. 2. Magazines and Newspaper cuttings. 3. Selections from other subject areas. 4. Recommended texts. 5. Supplementary readers. 6. Other resources e. g bulletin boards etc.
resources.assessment: Student to identify accurately, main ideas from the passages.

resources.title: Parts of Speech: Nouns, Verbs and Adjectives
resources.description: Theme: GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY JSS 1 | Content: 1.Nouns 2.Verbs 3.Adjectives
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. identify the features of nouns, verbs and adjectives in a given passage; and 2. list the functions of nouns, verbs and adjectives in the passage.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the features of nouns, verbs and adjectives and their functions, 2. Guides students to identify nouns, verbs and adjectives in given passages. 3. Guides students to make sentences with nouns, verbs and adjectives.

Students: 1. Listen attentively to the teacher. 2. Identify and give the functions of nouns, verbs and adjectives in given sentences. 3. Make sentences with nouns, verbs and adjectives.
resources.resources: 1. Various passages 2. Course book 3. Substitution tables 4. Pictures/drawings
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. identify correctly the features of nouns, verbs and adjectives; 2. write correctly the functions of nouns, verbs and adjectives in a given passage; and 3. generate appropriate sentences using nouns, verbs and adjectives.

resources.title: Parts of Speech: Adverbs, Conjunctions and Prepositions
resources.description: Theme: GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY JSS 1 | Content: 1. Adverbs 2.Conjucntions 3.Prepositions
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. identify the features of adverbs, conjunctions and prepositions; 2. list the functions of adverbs, conjunctions and prepositions in a given passage; and 3. make sentences with adverbs, conjunctions and prepositions.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the features of adverbs, conjunctions and prepositions and their functions 2. Guides students to identify adverbs, conjunctions and prepositions in given sentences/passages 3. Guides students to make sentences with adverbs, conjunctions and prepositions.

Students: 1. Identify adverbs, conjunctions and prepositions in given sentences. 2. Make sentences with adverbs, conjunctions and prepositions.
resources.resources: 1. Various passages 2. Substitution tables 3. Sentence strips 4. Story books 5. Magazines/ newspaper cuttings.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. identify correctly the features of adverbs, conjunctions and prepositions; 2. identify correctly the functions of adverbs, conjunctions and prepositions; and 3. construct sentences using adverbs, conjunctions and prepositions

resources.title: Adverbials and Tenses
resources.description: Theme: GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY JSS 1 | Content: 1. identify features of adverbials and tenses from passages on: - Peace and dialogue - Human rights - Value orientation 2. Adverbials e.g. frequency: always, often, everyday. - Intensifiers e.g. so, such, very. - Manner e.g. polite, rude. 3. Tenses e.g. present, past and future.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. identify adverbials in a passage; 2. make sentences with adverbials; 3. identify the different tenses in a passage; and 4. make sentences with the tenses.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides students to read the given passages. 2. Guides them to identify adverbials and tenses. 3. Guides students to make sentences with adverbials and tenses.

Students: 1. Read the given passages. 2. Identify the adverbials and tenses from the passages. 3. Make sentences with adverbials. 4. Identify the tenses. 5. Make correct sentences using the tenses.
resources.resources: 1. Given passages 2. Manuals 3. Course book 4. Other relevant texts 5. Sentence strips 6. Newspaper and magazine cuttings.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. identify correctly adverbials; 2. make correct sentences using adverbials; 3. identify tenses correctly; and 4. make sentences correctly using the tenses.

resources.title: Active and Passive Verbs
resources.description: Theme: GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY JSS 1 | Content: 1. Identification of active and passive verbs from passages on: - Preventing HIV/AIDS - War against cultism - Dangers of examination malpractice - Drug Abuse etc. 2. Making sentences using active and passive verbs.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. identify the active and passive verbs; 2. list active and passive verbs; and 3. make sentences with active and passive verbs.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads students to read the given passages. 2. Guides them to identify the active and passive forms of verbs in the passages. 3. Leads them to list the active and passive forms of verbs. 4. Guides them to make sentences with active and passive verbs.

Students: 1. Read the given passages. 2. Identify active and passive verbs. 3. List active and passive verbs. 4. Make sentences with active and passive verbs.
resources.resources: 1.Various passages 2.Substitution tables 3.Course book 4.Supplementary readers 5. Magazines/newspa per cuttings.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. identify correctly active and passive verbs in given passages; 2. make correct sentences using active and passive verbs; and 3. generate appropriate sentences from given substitution tables illustrating the active and passive verbs.

resources.title: Introduction to Literature
resources.description: Theme: LITERATURE JSS 1 | Content: 1. Literature pieces 2. Types of oral literature. 3. Categories of written literature. 4. The ways literature reflects different aspects of culture.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. identify features of literature; 2. identify features of oral literature; 3. identify features of written literature; and 4. explain literature as a carrier of language and culture.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains literature to the students. 2. Leads the students to give examples of the types of oral literature. 3. Leads the students to give examples of types of written literature. 4. Leads students to distinguish the basic devices of literary composition.

Students: 1. Listen to the Teacher‘s explanation on literature. 2. Explain oral literature and its categories. 3. Explain written literature and its categories. 4. Identify the various ways literature reflects the moral values of the society.
resources.resources: 1. Story books on folktales, myths, legends and history of ancient people and places. 2. Short story books from different places in the country and outside. 3. Recorded audio/video tapes of tales, story sessions, drama and poetry readings.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. identify literature and its two major categories of oral and written; 2. narrate some folktales or songs as examples of oral literature; and 3. re-tell some short stories narrated in books or novels.

resources.title: Introduction to Folktales
resources.description: Theme: LITERATURE JSS 1 | Content: 1. African and Non- African tales. 2. Features and themes. 3. Didactic lessons 4. Entertainment 5. Magical features.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. identify features of folktales; 2. retell folktales. 3. explain the themes of folktales; and 4. identify the moral lessons to be learnt from folktales; and 5. narrate folktales.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Tells folktales to students. 2. Leads students to retell folktales. 3. Leads them to identify the moral lessons in tales. 4. Leads students to identify the features/themes of folktales. 5. Leads them to dramatise the folktales.

Students: 1. Listen to and retell folktales. 2. Explain folktales. 3. Identify the features/Themes. 4. Dramatize the folktales. 5. Narrate folktales.
resources.resources: 1. Story books on folktales. 2. Supplementary readers. 3. Recorded folktales. 4. Narrate folktales.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. identify two features and themes of folktales; 2. retell and explain correctly folktales; and 3. identify moral lessons learnt, and 4. narrate folktales.

resources.title: Introduction to myths and legends
resources.description: Theme: LITERATURE JSS 1 | Content: 1. African and Non- African tales comprising myths and legends. 2. Features/Themes of myths and legends. - magic - supernatural - superstition
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. identify features of myths/legends. 2. explain the themes of myths/legends; 3. retell myths/legends; 4. identify the moral lesson to be learnt from myths/legends; and 5. narrate any myths/legends.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Narrates myths/legends to students. 2. Leads students to retell myths/legends. 3. Guides students to explain the themes and features of some myths and legends. 4. Guides students to identify their moral lesson. 5. Guides them to narrate some myths/legends.

Students: 1. Retell myths/legends. 2. Explain myths and legends. 3. Identify the themes/features. 4. Identify moral lesson. 5. Narrate myths and legends
resources.resources: 1. Supplementary books. 2. Story books on myths and legends. 3. Recorded short stories. 4. Course book. 5. Other relevant resources.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. identify two features of myths/legends; 2. retell and explain the themes of myths/legends; 3. identify moral lesson learnt; and 4. narrate any myths and legends in their communities.

resources.title: Prose: Types and features.
resources.description: Theme: LITERATURE JSS 1 | Content: Types of prose: - Narrative - Descriptive II. Features - Plot - Characterization - Style - Setting - Theme
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. identify the types of prose; 2. list the features of prose; 3. differentiate between the two types of prose; and 4. write own stories using the types of prose.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads students to identify different types of prose 2. Guides students to list the features. 3. Engages them in discussion of the story line. 4. Guides them to write a song. 5. Leads students to make comments on the moral messages of a story.

Students: 1. Identify different types of prose 2. List the features. 3. Participate in discussion of a story line. 4. Write a story. 5. Identify the moral lesson of a story.
